scaffold_text: Seat the beta children close to you for one extra guided round.|Use one prompt at a time and wait before repeating.|Model the answer with gesture support before asking again.
Use short repeat-after-me phrases with the beta children first.|Accept one-word or gesture responses before asking for a fuller answer.|Echo the child response clearly for the whole group.
Demonstrate the movement slowly beside the beta children.|Break the movement into two smaller steps.|Offer hand-over-hand support only if the child is comfortable.
Pair each beta child with a calm peer for the first turn.|Give a clear turn cue using name, gesture, and eye contact.|Praise waiting, sharing, or imitation immediately after it happens.
Offer the beta children a simpler first mark, shape, or rhythm to copy.|Let them choose between two easy ways to participate.|Notice effort and exploration before asking for another attempt.
